raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Purpose
`:amd: (MI355 DPX) MoE Kernels` failed in shards 2-5 of the nightly [amd-ci#15747](https://buildkite.com/vllm/amd-ci/builds/15747). Each of these shards ran one case of `test_aiter_moe_sort_backend_dispatch_env_matrix_mxfp4` (added in #62976), and all four failed with `Expected this MXFP4 DSV4 shape to set aiter's internal output_aux flag`. Shard 1 passed only because pytest-shard placed none of the four cases there.

The test relies on aiter selecting a tuned DSV4 MXMOE kernel, which sets `output_aux`. aiter keys its tuned MoE configs by `(gfx, cu_num, ...)`, and `dsv41_fp4_tuned_fmoe.csv` only has `gfx950,256` rows. The DPX agents expose 128-CU partitions, so aiter falls back to a heuristic FlyDSL config without `output_aux`. No gfx950 MoE config in aiter has 128-CU rows.

This PR moves the step from `mi355_dpx` to `mi355_1` (full MI355X, 256 CUs). 

## Test Plan
Full MI355X (gfx950, SPX, 256 CUs), in the `rocm/vllm-dev:ci_base` image with aiter 0.1.26, vLLM at 617135eed3.
The whole step ran as in CI: its three commands from `test-amd.yaml`, 5 shards in parallel with one GPU each, and the `run-amd-test.sh` environment.
The DSV4 cases were also run on their own:
```bash
cd tests
VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1 VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_MOE=1 pytest -v -s kernels/moe/test_modular_kernel_combinations.py \
  -k test_aiter_moe_sort_backend_dispatch_env_matrix_mxfp4
```

## Test Result
| Shard | DPX, 128 CUs ([amd-ci#15747](https://buildkite.com/vllm/amd-ci/builds/15747)) | Full MI355X, 256 CUs |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | passed | passed (7.4 min) |
| 2 | failed (`[ck]`) | passed (10.2 min) |
| 3 | failed (`[auto]`) | passed (8.9 min) |
| 4 | failed (`[opus]`) | passed (11.8 min) |
| 5 | failed (`[adaptive]`) | passed (6.6 min) |

All 15 commands exited 0 on 256 CUs, with no other failures.

AI-assisted tooling was used to analyze the CI logs and to run the validation. The results and the change were manually reviewed.

- `/ci run` starts upstream CI; `/amd-ci run` starts AMD CI only.
- Run commands test your branch with every commit currently on its upstream target branch. If it is behind, the bot merges the target branch into it first (pull before pushing again). Append `--allow-stale` to a run command to test an outdated branch as is, at your own risk.
- `/ci retry` retries failed jobs in the CI build for the current PR head. If the current head has no CI build, it starts a new CI build for the current head containing only jobs that failed in the latest earlier CI build for this PR.
- `/amd-ci retry` retries failed jobs in AMD CI for the current PR head. Use `/amd-ci run` when the current head has no AMD CI build.
- `/ci cancel` cancels scheduled or running CI builds for this PR branch; `/amd-ci cancel` does the same for AMD CI only.

<!-- vllm-ci-authorized -->

## Claude Code Review

This pull request is from a fork — automated review is disabled. A repository maintainer can comment `@claude review` to run a one-time review.

Looks good but I have a small concern - there are 3 "kinds" of tests under this pool:
```
- pytest kernels/moe --ignore=...--ignore=test_modular_kernel_combinations.py ...   # bulk of MoE kernel tests
- pytest kernels/moe/test_modular_oai_triton_moe.py ...
- VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1 ... pytest kernels/moe/test_modular_kernel_combinations.py -k "not multigpu" ...   # ← only this one has the failure
```
Only the last one (`test_modular_kernel_combinations.py -k "not multigpu"..`) causes the issue. Could you check if it's worth moving only this failing one to the mi355_1 pool (or creating a new bk step) while retaining the rest two in the dpx pool? (dpx pool gives the concurrency benefit)
Could we get this merged to fix the CI breakage and the reorg suggestion can be addressed as a follow-on?
